Repository instructions

Source: AGENTS.md

Communication

Use plain English in explanations, progress updates, commit messages, documentation, package vignettes and articles, NEWS.md entries, GitHub issues and pull requests, and comments in code. Describe what happens, what causes it, and why it matters. Avoid compressed jargon and invented compound labels. Introduce a technical term only when it helps, and explain its meaning first. Preserve scientific precision through concrete descriptions, equations or examples—not unexplained terminology. Assume the reader understands statistics but should not have to decode your shorthand. Before sending or saving text, replace any phrase that would reasonably prompt “What does that mean?” with a direct explanation.

State what the evidence shows. Add a limitation only when it materially changes how the reader should interpret or use that result. Connect it to a specific claim or decision in the surrounding text, and explain its practical consequence. Do not introduce an unasked alternative claim merely to disclaim it. Omit generic cautions about causality, uncertainty or generalisation when they add no useful information.

When reviewing a qualification, ask: “What misunderstanding does this sentence prevent, and has the surrounding text given the reader a reason to have it?” If there is no concrete answer, delete it.

Plot annotations

Keep default plots free of implementation and methodological commentary.

  • Preserve the established caption format. Adding a feature does not authorize expanding plot annotations.
  • Include labels needed to read the plotted values: axes, units, legends and established basis or constraint labels.
  • Do not repeat settings the user requested, or add interval sources, calibration details, numerical diagnostics, provenance or generic caveats.
  • Put those details in documentation, returned metadata or diagnostic output.
  • Before adding text, ask: “What specific misreading of this figure would this prevent?” If there is no concrete answer, omit it.
  • Review rendered plots for unnecessary text before delivery, just as you review them for incorrect values.

Starting new work

Unless the user explicitly instructs otherwise, always start new work on a new feature branch created from main. Use the gls/ branch prefix.

Before creating the branch, check the current branch and working-tree status. Create the feature branch with main as the explicit starting point, for example:

git switch -c gls/descriptive-name main

Do not branch from the current feature branch or carry unrelated work into the new branch. Preserve uncommitted changes without discarding or including them in unrelated work. If the user asks to continue an existing branch, reuse it.

Before merging into main, inspect the commits and diff relative to main and verify that the merge includes only the intended work. Resolve any accidentally inherited commits before merging.

Documentation topics and the pkgdown reference index

When adding a documentation topic, update the reference index in pkgdown/_pkgdown.yml in the same change. Place each public topic in the appropriate reference section. For a topic intended only for internal use, mark it with @keywords internal in its roxygen source instead.

Before committing, check that every new public topic is included in the index and validate the reference index with pkgdown. A missing topic causes the website build to fail.

Running tests

Run all package tests and checks outside the sandbox from the outset, including targeted tests and the full test suite. Request elevated execution with sandbox_permissions="require_escalated" for test commands; do not first attempt them inside the sandbox. Parallel-worker tests need local socket permissions that the sandbox blocks, so a sandboxed run can produce misleading failures and require an unnecessary rerun. This instruction does not bypass tool approval requirements.
